comment: Declared surfaces whose merge, in a repo where merging triggers automation on the
default branch, PERFORMS a real-world action rather than publishing code: it
provisions/mutates/destroys billable infrastructure, moves money, or is one-way.
Read by ai/bin/blast-radius, which is called by integration-gate before a merge.
Patterns are deliberately GENERIC (no product repo is named here). This file
lives in ~/dev/custom and classifies other repos by reading them, never by
requiring anything to be committed into them.
Adding a pattern only ever WIDENS what is held for the owner, which is always
safe. NEVER narrow or remove a pattern to make a merge pass
(ai/blocks/ops/safety-checks.md) -- excluding a path to go green is the named
forbidden move, and here it would silently restore the exact hole this exists to
close. If a pattern is genuinely wrong, the OWNER decides, and the change cites
the evidence.
Matching (ai/bin/blast-radius -> match?): fnmatch with FNM_PATHNAME, FNM_EXTGLOB
and FNM_DOTMATCH, so `*` and `**/` reach dot-prefixed files and directories
(gen_saas's .pkg/prod/tf read COLD without it -- DND-422). A leading `**/` also
matches at the repo root, and a trailing `/**` matches at ANY depth below.

surfaces.why: merging applies it: provisions, mutates or destroys real, billable cloud resources
merging changes what EVERY future merge does -- the machinery that performs the action

comment: DND-589 (the DND-422 class): the patterns above name the CI CONFIG files,
but merge-time CI also EXECUTES other repo files by relative path, and
those decide what a merge does just as much. Measured: gen_saas's
post-merge.yml runs .pkg/prod/bin/deploy-guard.sh (the guard that refuses
stale prod deploys) and ships .pkg/prod/docker-compose.production.yml;
walt_ui's .gitlab-ci.yml includes backend/.pkg/gitlab/terraform-aws.yml.
All read COLD, so editing them bypassed the owner stop.
`.github/actions/**` and `**/action.y{a,}ml` are static: a local action is
deploy-automation wherever it lives. This key adds the DYNAMIC part: every
file named by path, at head, in a merge-time CI config -- a GitHub workflow
with any trigger whose later runs execute the merged code (the same
workflow_trigger the automation term uses: every event except the
pre-merge ones, see PRE_MERGE_EVENTS) and every GitLab CI file (GitLab absence is not
provable) -- is a hit, and so is every file named by one of THOSE,
transitively. A `uses: ./dir` naming a local action pulls in its whole
directory (Dockerfile, entry point). Only paths that exist at head count,
so a word that merely looks like a path matches nothing.
Bounds (each pinned by a self-test case, and each measured on walt_ui,
where the unbounded walk reached 372 files): only CI YAML, action
metadata and scripts are FOLLOWED (a data file a step reads is a hit, not
a source of further hits); YAML is read structurally, skipping subtrees
that select or cache files (`changes:`, `paths:`, `cache:` ...); script
comment lines are dropped; a bare name in a script resolves beside the
script, not at the repo root; `.md` is never a hit (documentation is not
executed). With them, gen_saas reads 45 files and walt_ui 61. (gen_saas read
12 until DND-590 made its workflow_dispatch ci.yml a root: that adds its CI
check scripts and, through paths those scripts name as data, mix.exs,
mix.lock and Dockerfile.)
known_gaps: Implicit build entry points are NOT followed: `make` reads Makefile, `mix`/`npm run` read mix.exs/package.json, `docker build .` reads Dockerfile, and none is named by path. They are the application's build definition, touched by every feature merge; gating them would gate every deploy. The captain's `Blast radius: IRREVERSIBLE` channel is their only cover.

A plain DIRECTORY named in CI (`cp -r .pkg/prod dest`, `cd apps/web`) is not expanded unless it holds an action.yml/action.yaml: expanding every named directory would gate every app change in a repo whose deploy `cd`s into the app.

A path an executed script names as DATA -- a grep pattern, an echo -- is a hit, since no lexical rule separates it from a path the script runs. This fails WIDE. Measured: walt_ui's backend/mix.lock is a hit because backend/bin/checks/self-test.sh greps CI for the string 'backend/mix.lock'.
A path built at runtime (a loop variable, string concatenation, an absolute runner path such as /home/runner/work/...) is not resolved.

The roots are a DENY-list of pre-merge triggers (pull_request, pull_request_review, pull_request_review_comment, merge_group), so a trigger that runs merged code (schedule, workflow_dispatch, release, pull_request_target, ...) or an unknown one is a root (DND-590). A workflow_dispatch run may be pointed at an unmerged ref by whoever dispatches it; that does not narrow the root, because the routine dispatch runs the default branch.

surfaces.why: merging RUNS it: the migration executes on the deploy that merging triggers, and irreversibly destroys data. Ecto reversibility restores the SCHEMA, never the rows -- `remove :col, :type` in a `change` block is auto-reversible in Ecto's sense and every value in that column is still gone the moment it runs. NEVER use Ecto-reversibility to downgrade a hit here.

comment: This surface is CONTENT-gated: a path hit alone is NOT a surface hit.
Routine migrations (create table, add column, create index) touch these
paths on every feature MR and must stay COLD.
Measured 2026-09-20 over 364 migrations in gen_saas + walt_ui: a naive
verb rule (drop|remove anywhere) flags 59 and is ~50% precise on walt_ui,
gating `drop constraint` x15 and `drop index` x4, which lose no data.
This rule flags far fewer, and only where rows are actually destroyed.
Content is read from the file AT HEAD (git show <head>:<path>), never
from diff text: a diff hunk may not show the `def down` line, which
would make the up/down distinction undecidable. A file absent at head
was DELETED and does not execute on deploy -- not a hit, but PRINTED,
never silently skipped. Any other read failure is a hit (fail closed).

exclude_first.why: dropping an index or a constraint loses no rows; it is mechanically rebuildable by its inverse. This exclusion is what keeps routine schema hygiene ungated.

match_line.why: drops a table and every row in it
drops a column and every value in it
a `drop` whose argument this rule does not recognise -- the argument is what decides whether rows are lost, so an unrecognised argument is UNDECIDABLE and fails closed

match_region.why: raw destructive SQL in an `execute`. Scanned region-wide, not per-line, so heredocs are covered.

known_gaps: A lossy `modify` (narrowing a column type so Postgres truncates on cast) is NOT detected. Most `modify` calls are benign (null, default) and no pattern separates them, so this is a NAMED gap rather than a silent one; the captain's `Blast radius: IRREVERSIBLE` channel is its only cover.
A `drop table` on a table created earlier in the SAME migration is a hit, though it destroys nothing. Rare; fails closed by design.

surfaces.why: merging changes which actions an owner's Slack click may approve (the owner approval grant allowlist); a button can never approve a widening of what buttons can approve, so no grant class covers this surface
